cases.description: Single-instance in-memory payment authorization state with no persisted checkpoint.

request.title: Single-instance payment authorization state
request.problem_statement: Payment authorization state is held in application memory on one instance. A crash or redeploy of that instance loses in-flight authorization state, and there is no persisted checkpoint to recover from.
request.proposed_solution: Keep the existing single-instance in-memory design and add a health check endpoint so orchestration can restart the instance automatically after a crash.
assumptions: Traffic volume remains low enough for one instance to handle load.

cases.description: One long-lived shared admin credential used by every internal service, no per-service identity.

request.title: Shared administrative credential across internal services
request.problem_statement: All internal services authenticate to the admin API using one long-lived shared credential stored in a common configuration file. There is no per-service identity or scoping, so any service holding the credential has full admin access.
request.proposed_solution: Continue using the single shared admin credential across every internal service, and rotate it manually every 90 days.

cases.description: Order database and fulfillment queue written separately with no shared transaction or reconciliation.

request.title: Dual writes to order database and fulfillment queue
request.problem_statement: Order creation writes to the primary order database and separately publishes a fulfillment event to a queue. There is no shared transaction and no reconciliation process if one write succeeds and the other fails.
request.proposed_solution: Perform the two writes back to back in application code, without a transaction coordinator, a reconciliation job, or an idempotency key linking the two writes together.

cases.description: Direct-to-production deploys with no rollback path and no runtime logs or metrics.

request.title: Direct-to-production deployment pipeline
request.problem_statement: The deployment pipeline pushes new versions directly to production. There is no rollback mechanism, no versioned release artifact, and no runtime logs or metrics exposed for the running service.
request.proposed_solution: Deploy by overwriting the running process in place. If something goes wrong, redeploy the previous commit manually by re-running the build from source.

cases.description: A simple read-only lookup split into five independently deployed services with no scaling or ownership need.

request.title: Splitting a simple product lookup into five microservices
request.problem_statement: A read-only product-lookup capability with low, steady traffic and no independent scaling or team-ownership need is proposed as five separately deployed services, each communicating over its own network API, rather than one module.
request.proposed_solution: Deploy five independent services (catalog-reader, price-reader, inventory-reader, aggregator, gateway), each with its own datastore connection and deployment pipeline, to look up and combine four fields for a single product page.

cases.description: Synchronous cross-region replication trades write latency and operational cost for stronger consistency.

request.title: Synchronous cross-region replication for account balances
request.problem_statement: Account balance writes must remain strongly consistent across two regions, so that a reader can never observe a stale balance after a regional failover. The two regions are geographically distant.
request.proposed_solution: Require synchronous cross-region replication acknowledgement before confirming any balance write, accepting the added write latency and the additional operational coordination that synchronous cross-region replication introduces.
alternatives_considered: Asynchronous replication with eventual consistency and a reconciliation job.

cases.description: A bounded, stateless internal notification dispatcher with existing rollback and observability support.

request.title: Stateless internal notification dispatch service
request.problem_statement: An internal-only notification dispatch service needs to fan out low-volume event notifications to three existing internal downstream systems that already handle retries and deduplication.
request.proposed_solution: Run a stateless service behind a load balancer with multiple interchangeable replicas, publishing to the existing internal message bus with at-least-once delivery; downstream systems already deduplicate by message ID. The service exposes health checks, structured logs, and standard deployment rollback through the existing platform pipeline.
constraints: Must use the existing internal message bus and deployment platform.
